title: Yesterday: telling what happened
goal: Tell a story about the past — with no past tense to build. Learn the time words that do the work, the linking words that hold a story together, and how to answer *Kok, kemarin ke mana?*
bekal: narrate a day out, in order, in the past
react to someone else's story the way Indonesians do

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Cerita akhir pekan
dialogs.intro: Monday morning. Rina wants to hear everything.

lines.speaker: Rina:
lines.text: Sarah, kemarin ke mana? Aku telepon, nggak diangkat.
lines.id: Sarah, where did you go yesterday? I called and you didn't pick up.
lines.literal: Sarah, yesterday to where? I phone, not be-lifted.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Maaf! Saya ke Bogor sama teman.
lines.id: Sorry! I went to Bogor with a friend.
lines.literal: sorry! I to Bogor with friend.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Naik kereta. Berangkat pagi, jam tujuh.
lines.id: By train. We left in the morning, at seven.
lines.literal: ride train. depart morning, hour seven.

lines.speaker: Rina:
lines.id: What did you do in Bogor?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Kami jalan-jalan di Kebun Raya. Bagus sekali!
lines.id: We wandered round the Botanical Gardens. It was beautiful!
lines.literal: we walk-walk at garden great. good very!

lines.speaker: Rina:
lines.text: Hujan nggak? Bogor kan kota hujan.
lines.id: Did it rain? Bogor is the rain city, after all.
lines.literal: rain not? Bogor you-know city rain.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Hujan, dong. Waktu itu kami sedang makan siang.
lines.id: Of course it did. We were having lunch at the time.
lines.literal: rain, indeed. time that we in-middle-of eat midday.

lines.speaker: Rina:
lines.text: Ha ha, selalu begitu. Makan apa?
lines.id: Ha ha, it always is. What did you eat?
lines.literal: ha ha, always like-that. eat what?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Soto ayam. Baru pertama kali dan langsung suka.
lines.id: Chicken soto. My first time, and I loved it straight away.
lines.literal: soto chicken. just first time and directly like.

lines.speaker: Rina:
lines.id: What time did you get back?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Sampai rumah jam delapan malam. Capek tapi senang.
lines.id: I got home at eight in the evening. Tired but happy.
lines.literal: arrive house hour eight night. tired but happy.

notes: **Not one verb in this dialogue is in a past form, because there are none.** *Berangkat*, *makan*, *pulang* are exactly the words you learned in Unit 5. What makes the story past is *kemarin* in the first line — and after that, everything that follows is understood to be past until something says otherwise.

**Ngapain?** is Jakarta-flavoured everyday speech for "what were you doing?" / "what for?". The standard form is *Sedang apa?* or *Melakukan apa?*, but *ngapain* is what you will hear from friends. Recognise it; use it once you are among friends.

**Sama instead of dengan.** *Sama teman* — "with a friend". *Sama* officially means "same", but in everyday speech it takes over the job of *dengan* (with). Both are correct; *dengan* is what you write.

**Kan is a whole word compressed into three letters.** From *bukan*, it means "isn't it, after all, you know". *Bogor kan kota hujan* = "Bogor is the rain city, as you know". Sprinkling *kan* into your speech is one of the fastest ways to sound less like a textbook.

**Waktu itu — "at that time".** This is how Indonesian sets a scene in the past. Combined with *sedang*, it gives you the equivalent of the English past continuous: *Waktu itu kami sedang makan* — "we were eating at the time".

grammars.title: The past, without a past tense
body: Everything is done by time words, and each one has a precise range.
after: ⚠️ **Tadi and kemarin are not interchangeable.** *Tadi* is strictly today; *kemarin* is strictly yesterday or thereabouts. Saying *kemarin* about something that happened this morning is a real mistake, and an easy one to make when your own language uses "earlier" for both.

**Dulu is memory, not yesterday.** *Dulu saya tinggal di Bali* means "I used to live in Bali" — the far past, a former life. Its other job you have already met: *dulu* after a verb means "first" (*Coba dulu* — try it first).

grammars.title: Holding a story together
body: Narration needs joints. These are the ones you will use in every story you ever tell.
after: *Oleh-oleh* deserves a note of its own: it means a small gift brought back from a trip for the people who stayed behind, and bringing one is a genuine social expectation in Indonesia. Come back from a weekend away with a packet of something local and you will have made a friend for the year.

blocks.text: Indonesian conversation is full of short reactions — silence while someone talks is felt as coldness. These are the noises to make.
💬 *Iya* is the everyday form of *ya*, and Indonesians often double it. Neither is stronger than the other; the doubling just adds warmth.

*Seru* means "exciting, fun, a good time" and it is the standard answer about anything from a weekend to a film. Its neighbours: *asyik* (enjoyable), *rame* (lively, crowded — and that is a good thing), *biasa saja* (nothing special).
💬 *Gimana* is spoken *bagaimana*. You will hear it far more often than the full form, and *Gimana?* on its own is a complete question meaning "well? how was it? what happened?".

items: Yesterday I went to Bogor.
I went by train with a friend.
We had lunch there.
Suddenly it rained.
I got home at eight in the evening.
I used to live in Bali.
Have you ever been to Papua?

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with tadi, kemarin, dulu or waktu itu.
items: ____ pagi saya ketemu Rina di kantor.
____ saya ke Bogor, hari Minggu.
____ saya tinggal di Bali, sepuluh tahun lalu.
____ kami sedang makan siang, lalu hujan.
Dia baru ____ pergi, lima menit lalu.
____ malam saya tidur jam sebelas.

exercises.prompt: React in Indonesian. Write what you would say.
items: Your friend says their phone was stolen.
Your friend says they got the job.
Your friend pauses in the middle of a story.
Your friend says they went to Bali for a week.
Your friend says the concert was cancelled.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: Bogor / kemarin / saya / ke
teman / naik / kami / sama / kereta
hujan / tiba-tiba / turun
malam / jam / rumah / delapan / sampai / saya
Bali / pernah / saya / ke

answers: Kemarin saya ke Bogor. — Saya naik kereta sama teman. — Kami makan siang di sana. — Tiba-tiba hujan. — Saya sampai rumah jam delapan malam. — Dulu saya tinggal di Bali. — Kamu pernah ke Papua?
